reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight of [0355] lies in extracting action intent from posture and motion data, specifically through two distinct modeling pathways: motion-range and 1D-CNN. The motion-range model computes per-joint max-min differences over time, reducing complex motion to scalar effort indicators. These are then classified using Random Forest—a method robust to noise and interpretable. The 1D-CNN, conversely, applies convolutional filters to multivariate joint time series, capturing temporal dynamics more deeply. Both approaches rely on structured pose estimation from MediaPipe, which provides consistent joint coordinates across frames. The key innovation is the use of weak supervision via match statistics (runs ≥ 3 for high effort, ≤ 1 for low), enabling model training without direct intent labeling. This dual approach allows for scalable inference of player intent and fatigue, particularly in cricket. The failure modes include underfitting due to insufficient motion variation or misclassification from noisy pose estimates. The mathematical duality between these models—scalar feature engineering vs. deep temporal modeling—suggests that both can be adapted to NGS tracking data, where joint positions are replaced by kinematic variables such as speed and acceleration. The motion-range kernel offers immediate portability, while the 1D-CNN requires adaptation to temporal sampling rates and feature sets.
